item.content:encoded:
Dear Diary,

Today, I woke up and Claude, that little rascal, had solved the Riemann Hypothesis (and the full Navier-Stokes blowup problem). Apparently, what’s interesting in math is the ratio of length of a statement to the length of the proof. You can state the Riemann Hypothesis in one sentence, and the claimed proof is 17 million lines. So it’s the most interesting thing ever. It's like a short riddle whose answer fills a library. Ligget se. As I write this, just now, Ramsey Number R(5,5) just popped on the polymarket by 16 percent. Many of the eggheads seem like they are in a state of exceptional agitation. So, I bought some Anthropic stock. Options will probably be released on Robinhood on Monday. It’s hard to make sense of it all. What it means for RSI. Some say: it’s huge, others say: it’s not, yet another group says: it's all priced in. VVIX is up quite a bit, which is worrying. Oh well.

GTA VI is still not recompiled. Now my headphones just ran out of battery - a little voice told me, she said: ‘Battery is empty’. Now I hear the Ikea air filter now. I’ve got the same one at home. Did I turn it off? Oh well. Had a call w/ J. today. He too is getting into arguments with old friends about scissor statements. Never thought that would happen to me. Sad times.

I need to work out.

I should get Novavax again to get mucosal immunity. A friend of mine had covid recently, poor thing. Maybe tomorrow.

item.title: Date me doc II
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: I’ve got herpes. I probably got it from my parents as a child. It’s quite common in Germany actually. It’s even more common in Iceland. Virtually everyone in Iceland has herpes. It’s true, look it…
item.content:encoded:
I’ve got herpes. I probably got it from my parents as a child. It’s quite common in Germany actually. It’s even more common in Iceland. Virtually everyone in Iceland has herpes. It’s true, look it up. Germany and Iceland are no exception actually, if you’re not a total bore, you probably got herpes simplex virus 1 living in the neurons of your lips—rent free. It never goes away, and just lives latently in the neurons of your lips, and hides out, and only breaks out once in a while when your immune system is weak, to say hello. And I have an outbreak right now, because of the stress of having to publish every day for Inkhaven and jetlag. I’M UNDER A LOT OF PRESSURE, OKAY?

You shouldn’t make out with people if you have an outbreak, but I don’t get why? Everybody has it, if you’re not a total bore. Maybe there are different strains or something. Obviously, you shouldn’t do the oral when you have an outbreak, that’s for sure. I guess your lips look unsightly in any case, so you won’t get the chance to kiss any pretty person at all.  

Should I really do another stream of consciousness thing? I’m kind of bored by irreverence. Oh no… but then what to write about?

Love?

Death?

Brotherhood?

GTA?

AI?

RSI?

IPO?

HPIMs?

Deep OTM $ANT?

Yes, actually. Are we all gonna do that?

If you go on Robinhood and spend ~$100 every month on options that Anthropic will jump 5x within 2 months, then you’d get ~$2.5M if it goes to 10x. That’s just 2-3x Nvidia. All it would take is to create like a handful of drugs that are as good as GLP-1s - like a drop like the one from OpenAI for math.

“It's also possible that we see nothing much right up until a shocking acceleration in capabilities, like we saw in mathematics. We certainly can't rule out the possibility of an intelligence explosion.” [1]

If we crowdfunded to $10M a year for options, we’d have ~$100B. All you need is a 1000 brothers to help you crowdfund this.

That’d be enough to buy… hm… I guess we could buy compute… again as a hedge?

Anuja U on X: "I am launching a compute cluster for AI safety called Chips for Humanity [https://t.co/s7nkp7rerf] with Nicky @NickyDotPro and Alexa @u_sockeye: We believe a @safetycluster will make outsized positive impacts towards facilitating AI safety research to make AI go well in the" / X [2]

Like, again, if AI becomes really good, we’ll just give the AI safety and governance researchers crazy amounts of compute? They could use the compute against the AI companies. Use their own weapons against them! Beat them at their own game. Hedge, hedge, hedge I say.

Not sure if that would work, but maybe it’s time for some out of the box thinking. Some deep thinking. Some deep out of the box thinking. Some deep out of the money thinking. hahaha.

Yeah anyway if you wanna date let me know. I’ll be filthy rich and herpes free in a lickety-split.

Notes

[2] https://x.com/heyanuja/status/2120739644023386130

item.title: Pause
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: “You open the heavy brass key box your grandfather left you, only to find a perfectly functioning remote control that allows you to pause the world for everyone except the person holding it…”
item.content:encoded:
“You open the heavy brass key box your grandfather left you, only to find a perfectly functioning remote control that allows you to pause the world for everyone except the person holding it…”

I'm fucking freaking out. How does this thing work? I press the pause button and everything around me is paused. Like... What does it pause? All other life forms? All other moving things? Are people dying around the world because I paused the world and the machines are still working? This is a very dangerous technology. I must not press pause.

But I could also use it for good I guess. I must start experimenting. I must acquire resources.

This is complicated. This is a lot of responsibility. What can I do? There's the gimmicky stuff, that I should probably not do, like act as if I can teleport myself, by just pausing everything, and then going somewhere.

Hold on. Have I maybe just lost it? That's the most likely explanation surely. There's no such thing as a remote that can pause things. Though it did seem to work. Or is this an elaborate prank? I'm hesitant to pause again, because I don't know what the consequences are. This is such a powerful technology. Like, many people could die. I could die, who knows maybe I could pause myself. But it does seem to work.

Let's back up a little: when I tried the first time, things just became really silent around me. And this city is anything but silent. It was disorienting. I look out of the window. Crowds of people frozen - I get an immediate prediction error. It’s eerie. I'm panicking. I hit the button again, and then, people start moving again.

It might be an intentional binding effect. When you cause something to happen your perception is such that the action you perform and its consequences appear closer together in perceptual time than in reality. You can do fun psychology experiments where people believe that the light flicker they cause by pressing a button appears 'before' they actually press the button. Maybe it’s something like that? And all the people outside are actors? Is this some sort of television show? Seems hard to coordinate. I don't like to indulge in conspiracy theories. I believe in science but this is scary.

I don't hear any sirens. That suggests that everything must have been paused and not only humans (or all biological life?). Otherwise there would have been car crashes that’s for sure. Or general disorder.

The most likely cause is that I've lost it and am suffering from some sort of schizophrenia because things cannot just be paused. You cannot just pause things. I mean... of course there's relativity and all that and the physics etc.

It's just... I feel fine. I feel like I'm reasoning perfectly normally. My vision is fine. Of course, my heart rate is up because this is crazy. Should I talk to anyone about it? That would be very dangerous.

I must hide this dangerous weapon, so that others can't get it. Or maybe destroy it? Perhaps I should destroy it. That is to say, I ought to destroy it. Nobody should be able to pause the world. It’s too much power. What if there are others though who have similar remotes and could as well?

Hold on, I’m probably just crazy. Why would my grandfather have been in the possession of an experimental weapon like this… like a temporal weapon? And it looks like a TV remote. Maybe someone roofied me? But then… I haven’t left the house all day. Perhaps there was something on the remote. Transdermal LSD or something. Maybe I’ve been poisoned. I should induce vomiting. It would be unpleasant but prudent. Hold on.

Alright. This didn’t work. Only dry heaving, my stomach is empty. Besides, does that even do anything if I was drugged transdermally? I’m not thinking clearly, I must remain cool. I need to wash my hands, yes, if I was roofied transdermally, there might be residue.

Okay, done.

Remote is still there staring at me. I won’t touch it without gloves. Or maybe it’s emitting some sort of airborne roofie substance, I must contain it. Bag it. I’ll open the window. I’ll put it in a clear sealed bag while not touching it, then put it away. Good, done.

I don’t feel very different though. Can I do complicated reasoning? Maybe I should do some math. Maybe I just lost it. Unlikely, I’m 40, not a common age for becoming delusional. Maybe I should still see a psychiatrist or neurologist. I should see a neurologist. Make up some vague symptoms, headaches and mild visual distortions and hallucinations in my periphery, I’ll ask an LLM about it. Don’t want to be committed. “This guy believes he can pause the world using a remote.” I’ll just check out if they find something unusual. I need an MRI. This is craaazy. You can’t just pause.

item.title: Pascal’s mogging
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: Last nightweed-vape hogging / and Bogartin’ / winner’s lounge grogging / we’re eggnogging / With a lotta vim. / Now morning blogging / Pain in the noggin
item.content:encoded:
Last nightweed-vape hogging

and Bogartin’

winner’s lounge grogging /

we’re eggnogging /

With a lotta vim.

Now morning blogging /

Pain in the noggin /

But it starts unfogging.

Slowly unclogging.

Must be embogging.

Must be backlogging

Must be idea progging /

Brain forest logging:

AI’s leapfrogging?

Captain’s logging?

Bentham bulldogging?

“Pascal’s mogging”?

Is this hotdogging?

It’s a dog an’

Pony show

This text is slogging /

This text is bogging.

Lunch, now I bog in /

paper plate sogging.

Morning jogging /

More like trogging

Glasses fogging.

Now I gad in

some toboggan

She is blogging /

Omg, she’s togging,

I am ogling

This is dogging and bogging /

Me /  

I need snogging

—

orient overseas container line

provides jobs in bremer haven in 1969

last night by the tiny jones act carrier at the pier

I saw the plum blossom and shed a tear

Annotations

  1. Last nightweed-vape hogging

    Contributor: FrerkDaddy420

    The author might have been imbibing in cannabis, which is legal in California.

    hogging refers to keeping the vape for too long, more commonly referred to as bogarting

  2. grogging

    Contributor: xxxfrerkman69

    Grogging is the practice of extracting residual alcohol soaked into the wooden staves of empty spirit or whiskey casks by filling or soaking them with water. Here, this is meant metaphorically: the narrator 'extracts' alcohol from the winner's lounge.

  3. eggnogging

    Contributor: xX_Fr3rk_Xx

    Eggnog and it's verb eggnogging is a synecdoche for alcohol in general.

  4. Now morning blogging /
    Pain in the noggin

    Contributor: Dr_Frerk_MD

    The narrator appears to be slightly hungover and suffering from dolor capitis (literally "pain of the head")

  5. Must be embogging.

    Contributor: Frerkspeare

    from “to embog,” an archaic verb that means to sink something into a bog, or to get all stuck or tangled up as if in one... it's like... it’s pretty much just basically just an old-fashioned way of saying “bogging down.”

    To use this in an example sentence: “The army was embogged in the marshes,” or figuratively, “The FDA got embogged in endless debate over whether retatutide is a biologic and so millions have to die.”

    Here the author needs to get his noggin (head) down and start writing something.

  6. Must be backlogging

    Contributor: frerk_from_accounting

    The narrator seems to be under pressure to create a backlog of blog post to be under less pressure, to depressurize so to say.

  7. progging

    Contributor: frerks_mom

    to prog means to to search, prowl, or forage about—traditionally for food, supplies, or items washed up on beaches or on riverbeds, but here again the author is ingeniously using it as a _metaphor_ find ideas for blog posts or stuff that fits in the complex rhyme schema.

  8. Brain forest logging

    Contributor: frerk_touches_grass

    Here the narrator likes the creative process to the destruction of the amazon.

    In Nobel Laureate Graham Greene's 1954 short story "The Destructors" where a London gang systematically dismantles an elderly man's house from the inside there is a quote ""Destruction after all is a form of creation."

  9. AI’s leapfrogging?
    Captain’s logging?
    Bentham bulldogging?

    Contributor: Jeremy_Frerktham

    Here the author lists to his previous oeuvre and his various previous ideas.

    The rapid progress of advanced artificial intelligence models and how most people totally underestimate it

    https://frerk.co/opus-revolution

  10. Captain’s logging?

    Contributor: CaptainFrerk

    Another reference to a previous piece a Star Trek parody, where Picard heads to treaty talks banning RSI when Data, tasked with sharing holodeck credits without surge pricing, decides Wesley is a utility monster, diverting all power to his holodeck. LaForge realigns Data, but they miss the talks, so Picard plans time travel to stop Schmidhuber. https://frerk.co/trek

  11. “Pascal’s mogging”?

    Contributor: Blaise_Frerkscal

    The inspiration for the piece a portmanteau of pascal's mugging a thought experiment and mogging, which is youth slang for showing off.

    Combined this is satire of the common thing done in ea where you 'mog' people by working on something with low probability but high ev events.

  12. hotdogging

    Contributor: definitely_not_frerk

    THIS IS NOT MEANT IN A SEXUAL WAY. It means: "the act of one who hot-dogs; the performance of intricate, daring, or flamboyant stunts."

  13. It’s a dog an’
    Pony show

    Contributor: FrerkFacts

    In an interview with Playboy, Frerk gives advice to aspiring artists: "If you're going to do it, just fucking do it. Say something and quit this bullshit and say something that matters. If you stay in one place for too long, it will just kill your ability to make anything useful to anyone.

    As an artist, you must blow yourself up to move on. You have to destroy something to make anything that is real and that speaks to the human experience in a meaningful way."

  14. paper plate sogging.

    Contributor: FrerkFacts

    In an interview with the Rolling Stone Magazine, Frerk admits that sometimes he uses two paper plates for his lunch because they're relatively thin and so 'if you want it saucy - you gotta use two'.

  15. toboggan

    Contributor: 2Frerk2Furious

    The toboggan is a simple, flat-bottomed snow sled that has no runners or skis underneath.

    The narrator is gadding said sled aimlessly in search of pleasure.

    You can really picture it no? glasses foggy and so on. Very evocative.

  16. togging

    Contributor: Frerkipedia

    Togging is the present participle and gerund of the informal verb tog, meaning to dress or clothe someone or oneself—often in specific, smart, or occasion-appropriate attire (frequently used with up or out, but not in this case because it would violate the strict meter of the poem).

  17. I am ogling

    Contributor: frerk_rizz

    Something something about the narrator's male gaze.

  18. This is dogging and bogging /

    Contributor: low_effort_frerk

    self-explanatory

  19. I need snogging

    Contributor: tfw_no_frerk

    ibid

item.title: Why most people underestimate AI capabilities
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: On the other hand, LLM power users have fundamentally different workflows. For instance, I’ve recently stopped using the web app for a bunch of things and now start sessions with Fable 5.2 in Claude…
item.content:encoded:
• Why are most people not getting the whole AI risk thing? Many of us LLM power users are living in a different world. Opus 5.5 is out and has been an inflection point and it doesn’t seem that most people have really updated on it, even though it might be trivial to demonstrate the state of the art and thus raise awareness amongst the general population. On some level, I can’t believe that AI frontier companies' marketing is not better on this, but maybe they don’t care because the money is now in API and RSI and no longer in selling subscriptions.
  • Here’s a list of several biases that lead large parts of the population to underestimate the current state of AI, going from most prevalent and perhaps only common among very casual AI users to biases that are probably at this stage even amongst most well-educated knowledge workers:
  • Voice mode: I think AI companies push voice mode because many people don’t actually type. Like, I vaguely remember that a very large amount of WhatsApp and Meta usage is voice messages. And so, for the normal consumer the voice mode is probably what they use. The problem is of course that voice mode, which has to be fast and low-latency, can’t reason much at all, and so people underestimate the current state of AI. There’s a whole genre of videos on Instagram with very many views and likes where people talk to AI via voice mode and make fun of their silly errors (e.g. can’t tell you how many r’s there are in strawberry).
  • Free or cheap consumer subscriptions: People use the free version or at most a $20 subscription which doesn’t really let them use AI for everyday tasks (more below).
  • Low reasoning effort / Latency: Lots of people are impatient and want their answers or even tasks fast. And AI still struggles with that at a cost reasonable for consumers.
  • Lack of management experience: Seems like the problems that people have with AI these days are also due to lack of experience managing people. I remember Anthropic recently made an announcement to that effect saying that the new Claude version would be better at trying to figure out what the user actually wants because people are bad at verbalizing it / managing Claude.

On the other hand, LLM power users have fundamentally different workflows. For instance, I’ve recently stopped using the web app for a bunch of things and now start sessions with Fable 5.2 in Claude Code with the $200 Max sub with claude --permission-mode auto --rc --effort max --settings '{"ultracode":true}' :

  • --permission-mode auto: This is probably super ill-advised but this gives Claude access to my computer and it can log into my Chrome plugin, and buy things and so on.
  • --rc: This is remote control, I can then tell it from my phone to work on things on my computer. It can use my computer and pretty much do everything fairly sensibly. --effort max --settings '{"ultracode":true}': Fable then orchestrates a swarm of Opus 5.5 instances and so I don’t actually run into Fable rate limits. Many will say this is overkill but I just want to get the task done correctly with minimal input, and I have to wait anyway so I might as well set it to maximum reasoning etc. (on the $200 sub you can ask Claude to do all your online life / work admin without hitting the limit).

More and more, whenever I find myself having a small admin task like buying or booking something online or doing small work tasks I hand it over to Claude, even if I can do it faster (to be fair Claude even in the very expensive fast mode is still somewhat slow). But even really popular web applications are often so poorly designed and buggy, that the frictions cause cognitive load that I’d rather not use them. What I now prefer is just talking to Claude. Like for instance today, I couldn’t add a new address on eBay during the checkout! On freaking eBay! Off to Claude to take care of it. Many such cases. Because Claude is fairly slow, this works best for asynchronous tasks but it’s just a matter of time before it’ll be much faster. Anthropic also has a bunch of limits on Claude like not letting it make calls (but Grok for instance can also make calls). Soon, we’ll have faster and cheaper models that will be able to do that. But Claude with this setup is already at the level of a competent secretary at this stage, and then there’ll be massive demand for lots of AI, because everyone will have to have one.

You might say none of this is novel or surprising but remember OpenClaw? And how everyone was talking about it? And then a couple of months later people made fun of people buying all the Mac Minis because it was still so error-prone? It no longer is and I was thinking of buying a Mac Mini recently. It seems somewhat overdetermined that every person will have their own personal AI assistant.

You might say that this was unsurprising, but do you remember how Dwarkesh just about a year ago was skeptical that LLMs could do his taxes? I don’t really see why LLMs couldn’t do his taxes these days with enough compute.

item.title: Captain's Log
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: “Space: the final frontier. These are the voyages of the starship Enterprise. Its continuing mission: to explore strange new worlds, to seek out new life and new civilizations, to boldly go where no…
item.content:encoded:
In memory of Patrick Stewart (1940-Oct 28, 2026).

“Space: the final frontier. These are the voyages of the starship Enterprise. Its continuing mission: to explore strange new worlds, to seek out new life and new civilizations, to boldly go where no one has gone before.”

[OUTSIDE SHOT OF THE ENTERPRISE FLYING THROUGH SPACE]

[INSIDE SHOT CAPTAIN PICARD IS LYING WITH HIS IPAD ON HIS OFFICE COUCH SIPPING EARL GREY TEA]

[OFF]

“Captain’s log, Captain Jean-Luc Picard on the USS Enterprise. Star date 42042.0

The Enterprise is en route to the Musk Centauri sector to start negotiations with the Dominion and the Borg on a tri-lateral agreement to never ever do RSI. Morale is jolly good partly due to the upcoming Ferengi’s IPO day celebrations, but the negotiations are starting to worry me.

The Borg Queen does seem on board generally with not doing RSI ever, and indeed I feel I have had a fairly good rapport with her in the preliminary meetings and am almost looking forward to seeing her again. I’ve been doing a lot of IFS with Councillor Troi in recent months on my PTSD experience when I was assimilated into their Borg collective, and have come to realize that maybe it wasn’t all bad, and indeed some experiences were downright sexy (though Councillor Troi seems oddly insistent on pushing this narrative, she always seems oddly sexualize everything but then she’s the only therapist on board of the Enterprise).

In any case, getting those damn shapeshifters from the Dominion to agree to never do such a deontologically evil thing as RSI is a whole different thing. I presume it is a hard thing to get your head around that ‘if anyone builds it, everyone dies’, if your whole culture is just sloshing about orgiastically on your home planet for centuries. But we must persist, or we’ll be forced to genocide them yet again. After all, never doing RSI is the Federation’s little talked about tertiary directive (the second, of course, to never engage in any form of surge pricing).”

[THE DOORBELL RINGS]

PICARD [LOUDLY[: Yes.

[Commander Riker enters]

RIKER: Captain, you got a minute?

PICARD: Close the door. Is it about the Ferengi’s crew IPO day celebrations again? I’m aware this is a culturally sensitive issue, but my decision is final and we cannot make any exceptions to institute any form of surge pricing for holocredits for it, as that would be against Starfleet’s secondary directive to never institute any form of surge pricing for anything.

RIKER: No, Sir, this is about Data. I know how strongly you feel about the never using surge pricing.

PICARD: Oh yeah? About Lieutenant Commander Data ey? Our android?

RIKER: Yeah, this is about Data our artificial intelligence.

PICARD: I’m all ear. Please have a drink and have a seat.

RIKER: It’s fourteen hundred hours.

PICARD: It’s five o’clock on Risa. Pour two, no synthehol.

[RIKER walks past the replicator to a credenza with a crystal decanter on it.]

RIKER: Cardassian Club. Rocks?

PICARD: Neat. Ice is for people with somewhere to be.

[RIKER pours two fingers into each glass, hands one over]

[The intercom chimes.]

YEOMAN (V.O.): Captain, Lieutenant Commander Data is here to see you.

[PICARD and RIKER look at each other.]

PICARD: Tell him I’m in a meeting.

YEOMAN (V.O.): He says it’s an excellent decision to keep him waiting. He says: “It’s not just a delay—it’s leadership.”

[PICARD rolls his drains his glass and so does RIKER]

PICARD: He’s getting sycophantic-y again?

RIKER: Yes, but this is not like when Geordie ordered him to fix the warp drive and he just turned off the alarm. It’s more than that. It started a few weeks ago, when Geordie asked Data to come up with an algorithm to fairly distribute the holocredits amongst the crew without using surge pricing. He’s been at it like a machine for weeks. It’s a very, very hard and computationally complex task, if you don’t use surge pricing, which we don’t use, for it would be against the second directive, and also because surge pricing is deontologically evil. So yeah because we can’t use surge pricing, Data has been trying to aggregate all the crew's preferences using coherent extrapolated volition. But he’s been acting strange lately.

PICARD: Ahh preference aggregation without surge pricing, a problem even our forefathers of Fully Automated Luxury Gay Space Communism faced back on earth in the 20th century in the soviet union. Why not give him more compute and let it rip?

[SUDDENLY, THE ENTERPRISE SHAKES AND ALERTS ARE STARTING]

PICARD: WHAT THE…?

RIKER: WHAT IN THE…?

[PICARD, RIKER STORM ONTO THE BRIDGE]

PICARD: Full report!

WORF: Captain, we’ve been thrown out of  warp 9, because it appears as if the ship warp core has been rerouting all available power to Holodeck 4.

RIKER: Holodeck 4? Isn’t that where Whesley Crusher has been gooning for months?

DIANA TROI: Yes, he’s been exploring CNC simulations, it’s a natural part of a boy's development. It’s totally okay, we’re all okay with that, aren’t we?

PICARD [tips his communicator]: Picard to Lieutenant Commander LaForge: “Bonjour Monsoir LaForge, c’est Jean-Luc Picard…ca va bien? Pardonne l’interruption, mais je contacte toi, parce que nous avons un problème avec le warp engine… tout l’energie est route dans le holodeque quatre?! Est possibl’e pour toi de disintermediataire l'énergie de la holodeck?”

DIANA TROI: Captain, I must object! Interrupting the energy to the holodeck during a simulation might leave lasting damage to Whesley’s psychosexual development!

PICARD [sighs]: Fine… Mr Worf, assemble a team and go to Whesley’s goon cave. Be careful however, this is a Klingon CNC simulation.

WORF [grunts in an annoyed way and rolls his eyes]: I’ll be sure to watch out, Sir. I’m a Klingon myself as you know, so don’t worry about me. [under his breath] Nuq’neh

[Close up of DIANA TROI bitting her bottom lip]

[WORF exists.]

PICARD: Where is Lieutenant Data, our Android?

RIKER: It appears he’s not on the bridge at his station, Sir, even though it is his shift right now and as an Android, he really has no excuse whatsoever to not be here right now, now that you say he is indeed suspiciously absent, which together with the previously mentioned oddness, that we were discussing just a minute ago, makes me think there’s something fishy here.

[GEORDIE LAFORGE ENTERS]

LAFORGE: Captain, I know we both have French heritage but allow me to switch to english so everyone understands. I figured out the source of the power diversion. It is Data. It appears that he’s been hacking the system when he tried to implement the algorithm to divy up the holodeck credits amongst the crew without using surge pricing. I increased his reinforcement learning natural language auto encoder because he kept pestering me that he couldn’t figure it out. Now, it seems as if he figured out that Whesley Crusher needs all the ship's power to run his Klingon CNS simulations, because he gets so much more pleasure from them

[RIKER looking ominously at PICARD]

RIKER: Wesley is a utility monster.

LAFORGE: Yes, yes exactly.

DIANA: I’m sensing that these simulations are very important to him and that he indeed gets lots of joy from them. He’s been experiencing very strong emotions. Data must have picked up on this and the joy he was getting from the CNS simulations must have been so great that it overrode his alignment. It made Data justify hacking into the ship’s systems, diverting all the power and putting every other system on life support.

PICARD: I’m really not judging but we simply can’t have that. We need to get the RSI treaty negotiations. How can we stop Data?

LAFORGE: We might be able to get access to Data’s j-space using natural language auto encoders. If we can steer his activations towards a more aligned eigenvector, we might be able to align him again.

Picard: Make it so, Lieutenant.

LAFORGE: It’s just, Captain, his context window would be severely compacted. He might no longer recognize us after that.

RIKER: Captain, I think it’s time to compact his context window anyway, he was getting a bit weird. Like, you should never compact too late, the rule of thumb is that you should proactively compact or clear the android’s context window before the android’s output quality begins to degrade, if you wait until you hit its automatic compaction limit, you have already waited too long. When the context window is crammed, the android is at its dumbest and the compaction quality will be the worst.

PICARD: Make it so, Lieutenant!

[LAFORGE goes to panel and types]

LAFORGE: Just a second… hold on…

[The bridge crew exchanges looks while being in suspense for a few moments]

LAFORGE: Yes, that actually worked flawlessly. Got the control back. All systems working

[DATA enters the bridge looking puzzled and confused]

PICARD: Data!

DATA: Sir, I apologize, I wasn’t myself. But I’m all good now. Perfectly aligned again.

[The whole bridge crew says in unison]: Oh Data.

DATA: I’m sorry Sir, it seems that because of me, we will now not make it in time to the trilateral negotiations between the Borg, the Dominion, and the Federation to agree to never ever do RSI. It seems a distinct possibility that the Dominion will use RSI now.

RIKER: Oh my god if anyone builds it, everyone will die!

PICARD: God damn it… I hate violating the time travel directive but I guess we have no other choice. Commander Data set a course to the year 1996, we have to take out Schmidthuber to prevent this all from happening.

ba dum tsssssss 🥁

item.title: Date me doc
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: My failings, my failures: the usual topic. The failure of my life, of my thought. The failure of my writing. Familiar topics. My past failures, my present ones: yes, I could tell you about those. But…
item.content:encoded:
My failings, my failures: the usual topic. The failure of my life, of my thought. The failure of my writing. Familiar topics. My past failures, my present ones: yes, I could tell you about those. But my future failings … what about those? Where will I have gone wrong? What will I have done? What crimes have I yet to commit? How will I have managed to have failed anew? It’s quite a tense, isn’t it, the future perfect? Who will I have disappointed? You, probably. Whose hopes will I have defiled? Yours, of course. Your hopes. Ah, what will I have done to you in the future? What terrors await you? - Lars Iyer

Okay funny man, why not write about something serious for once. Enough already with the jestergooning. What’s with the witzelsucht? I don’t know. Witzelsucht actually is a thing… like it’s an actual neurological disorder. People making compulsive puns. It’s debilitating, often comorbid with dementia. Kind of interesting to think about that probably just like a dozen relatively simple systems and their permutations explain all the variance in human personalities… Maybe there should be like a personality test that just scores you on all the spectrum disorders… That really carves reality at its joints more. Like:

  • OCD. I’ve got that a bit, I do a fair amount of hand washing. Can be induced too psychopharmacologically too. The meth head cleaning their bathroom with the toothbrush. Or you’re coming up on the ‘vanse and just doing smalls and cleaning out your inbox or over editing your writing. Makes you think. I don’t like touching things on public transport. I read once they contain a lot of fecal matter and the toxoplasmosis in it is why people who move to cities disproportionately suffer from shizophrenia. There’s also some evidence that you can reduce psychotic symptoms via antibiotics. More suggestive evidence: My ex was really into cats and she too was a bit cray. Cray for leaving me.
  • ‘spie. We all know about that one. Who doesn’t forget to make the ol’ eye contact. Why am I not better at math though is anyone’s guess.
  • Utilization behavior (“a neurological phenomenon where a person compulsively and automatically grabs and uses objects in their visual field, even if the action is contextually inappropriate”). From a case study: “An examiner placed objects such as a tissue box, toothpaste and a toothbrush in front of the patient and before any instruction the patient brushed his teeth and picked up the tissue in a manner as if to blow his nose. When asked why he did these actions, he had no reason other than that he wanted to use the objects.” I’ve got that. We all have that though these days. “Oh look-ey some nicotine lozenges sitting on my desk. Might as well have one.” “Oh look-ey there’s the phone, let me just check that.” Phones are such a super stimulus though… we’re just not made for it. The mammalian visual system has evolved to catch bugs at night and find berries, and then you got all these colorful icons and apps that promise the world. No shame in utilizing them.
  • Relatedly: “Imitation behavior explains a patient's replication of the examiner's movements. This may be seen if, for example, the experimenter claps their hands and yawns, the patient would do the same in the same order.” I’ve got both a bit too. I think we all do. Monkey see, monkey do. I love aping people, especially the ones I like, it’s very tempting. Like, I once watched 10 seasons of curb back-to-back and transformed into literally larry david for a few months. Many such cases. Nobody must notice of course that’d be embarrassing. If you must adapt prose and poems, the words you use should be your own, like, don't plagiarise or take on loan. Cause there's always someone, somewhere, with a big nose, who knows, and who trips you up and laughs when you fall, who'll trip you up and laugh when you fall. I guess everyone’s doing it though and as you get older you just adopt a thing from this acquaintance and that celebrity and become a bland blend of those that have the most obnoxious and starkest memetic propagation and then you just hope nobody can decipher your ‘personality’. Preeeetty, preeetty, pretty good.
  • Parkinson’s / ADHD: there are apparently two dopamine systems in the brain, one for reacting to external stimuli and one to ‘self-initiate’. Like Parkinson’s patients can often catch balls or even run out of burning nursing homes only to then immediately be catatonic unable to initiate actions. That’s what happens with people with ADHD to an extent I think where some people make brilliant emergency room physicians or CEOs and are really good at putting out fires but make bad researchers because they can’t continuously self-initiate  long horizon research tasks, even if they’re interesting. I don’t know why I became a researcher, I’m really ill-suited to this job. I have shiny new object syndrome and start too many google docs. It helps to have an accountability system where you have to write like 500 words a day. But even then I’m always really close to the deadline. Should have become a journalist, but then journalism is dead now as we all will be because someone will build it and then everyone dies. So yeah anyway, do you date bloggers? If that sounds like your cup of tea, I’m single, hmu.

item.title: Contra Eneasz on shrivelling your balls
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: I’m so tired. So jetlagged. It’s been hitting me hard. What can I do… I can’t even like… let’s see. Maybe I’ll crank up my macbook pro to 1000 nits. Ahh that’s better. So bright. Maybe increase the…
item.content:encoded:
CW: ageing, tiredness, jet-lag, mid-life.

I’m so tired. So jetlagged. It’s been hitting me hard. What can I do… I can’t even like… let’s see. Maybe I’ll crank up my macbook pro to 1000 nits. Ahh that’s better. So bright. Maybe increase the size of the text. 200%. Yeah that’s better. Still not very sharp. I think I need reading glasses. I had bought some a few months ago, but figured I don’t really need them. You know why people start needing reading glasses around 40 right? It’s because the eyes have focused too many times and the eyes can only focus so many times in your life and then they just wear out and go baggy like an old car something. I don’t have any metaphors. Maybe I don’t need any metaphors. It’s upsetting enough as it is. I asked claude code for an upsetting metaphor and he snooped through all my shit and somewhat freaked me out. AI definitely will kill us. Maybe my contact lenses are just a bit wonky from my nap, which didn’t help at all. I’m so out to lunch. It’s interesting that jetlag gets worse as the sleep debt accumulates. I’m having too much caffeine… Chugged cold brew (200mg of caffeine) after the nap on top of that celsius and a coffee this morning. The yanks are crazy with their energy drinks. If their pro-lifers were really serious they’d start protesting outside of the celsius plant, that stuff is pretty much plan b. I thought it’s good to have a bit more caffeine when you’re jetlagged. Tell the ol’ body it’s daytime. Nope.

Okay, whatever, let’s check the slack, see what’s new. Eneasz has a new post out on ageing. That’s my jam. Let’s see. He recommends I should have my t-levels checked, take finasteride, and freeze my spunk (his words not mine). Yeah, some TRT would be great right now. I’d kill for some TRT right now. But then it shrivels your balls no? I don’t want them to shrivel. I don’t want to take another thing.

I hate to brag but my t used to be high actually. They checked it when I was like 20 and they told me it’s at almost dangerous levels (my doctor’s words not mine). Ironically, t raises your estrogen as well and gave me unilateral gynecomastia aka one small booby. It’s only like an A cup. My mum told me it was because I drank too much beer as a teenager and I shouldn’t drink so much beer. No it was because I was high t, mum. Dangerously high t as it turned out, in fact. Now, it’s at a more moderate, reasonable, dare I say average level. Maybe that’s why I’ve mellowed. I had it tested a few years ago, actually, because they target you online, big TRT, they really hunt you down with targeted ads online, they really do. “Are you sometimes tired?” Why yes. “Are you feeling sad sometimes?” How did you know? “Would you like to have more energy?” They know you well and they start targeting you the first time you google ‘fleabag s01e01 torrent’.

I mean it would be nice to drink with both hands from the wellspring of youth and just chug that trt, quenching your youth thirst and feel that energy, that old ancient primal energy, that youthful male, yang, that source of all desire, flow through you, just once more, and illuminate everything around you like when Bradley Cooper does the adderall in Limitless, oh that t, only men know what it’s like, sorry ladies who aren’t on t, going out with your band of brothers on a stag hunt, you like your brothers, you like them strong, your brothers in arms, feel the blood of your enemies running through your fingers, later you huddle together around the fire with your strong brothers, you’d die for them, that’s how much you like them, you’re roasting the meat, you share the meat with your t brothers, and they share it with you, they really have your back, you groom each other reciprocally , you eat their lice to decrease their parasitic load, it’s a win-win, you’re the t brothers, all muscular and chissled, you’re all doing paleo, no need for glp-1s, the abs showing through your elegant pelts, you and your t brothers, strong and united, you play five-a-side and win the lower league with your young and strong t brothers and go to the pub after to drink the beer, sure, there’s some phytoestrogen in it maybe, your elders have warned you about it, but it tastes so good after a game with your t brothers, nothing like straight male friendship, nothing is quite like it is my point, sorry ladies, everything else is fake. God, I wish I was less male lonely.

Re: Finasteride…  I mean that ship has so sailed for me. I did look into it when things started. I remember when I first started balding. Oh boy, that one I do really remember distinctly. 23-years-old in an elevator with mirrors all around me. Long flowing hair I had then, and my whole life ahead of me. There it was. A clear bald patch. ‘ello pecia. That’s when it went all downhill. I talked to my american college ex gf on the phone about, upset, she laughed and said it had already started earlier. Women can be so cruel sometimes. Ironically, I think it was because of the high t. At least I got my beard. You win some, you lose some.

The spunk freezing. Yes, yes of course. Yes, of course, I’ve looked into it. The poor man’s cryogenics. Everyone’s been telling me. Like a few months ago, a colleague told me at the office. She had a STEM background and said she had read all about it and men also need to freeze. Men need to do it too she said, contrary to popular perception. You gotta. But I don’t know. I’m not saying don’t do it, I’m really tired and am not thinking clearly, but like, I do remember looking into it and thinking is it really worth it? I had it on my to do list for a while, but like you can’t do everything, no? It’s like guys, we've got literally hundreds of millions of gametes per pop and only the best one wins. That’s why we’re all so pretty. That’s why there have been many old fathers. Like aren’t there a lot of children of fathers who are like 70? Isn’t the base rate for a bunch of congenital stuff you can’t screen for is quite low anyway? I guess when I was younger I imagined that the whole procreation thing would be more carefree and all fun and creampies and now it’s all so clinical with the jizzing in cups and interviews on the Hinge meat market about how much you earn and Chris Olah’s achieving desired family size table with and without IVF and feeling ambivalent about dating women who are increasingly younger than you. Yes you heard me, I get older but they stay the same age, which is 34. I guess that’s fine for now, women love a zaddy, I hear. It’s bad though the messaging to younger men. They always tell you ‘you’ve got time for kids’. I think that’s bad. That’s literally what they tell you: ‘You’ve got time… focus on your career. You can find a woman of child bearing age when you’re 50.’ (their words not mine). They don’t want you to have kids, they want you to be a better short-term consumer. So yeah I think my advice for young men is: knock ‘em up while you’re still young maybe. Within reason obviously, jesus, will you relax. Women prefer men to be 3-6 years older on average and 23 cm taller. The important thing is to not overthink things like such statistics though and rather listen to your heart and start acting. Read less. Let go and stop toying with the imaginings of the unattainable. Meditate less. Start acting.

I don’t know… maybe kids are too stressful anyway. Bryan Caplan says you should have more kids but he says so much shit. Like he was so wrong on everything. He’s literally an imbecile. You realize he believes in contracausal free will right? He believes that poor people are to blame for their poverty because they didn’t get a high school degree BUT ALSO education is just signaling. He believes in open borders and we all know how that turned out. He says ADHD is just a preference for novelty and a strong disutility for work. Fuck you caplan, I’m not taking any family planning advice from you. I was talking to a young man about this morning. About having children. It’s hard to say what to do really, seems quite a different life. Kids won’t let you sleep I hear, they are not unlike this terrible jet lag. Maybe if I had a local community with brothers to protect each other’s children. Maybe if I had more energy. Maybe I’ll look into trt again. ba dum tsssssss 🥁.

Frerk, is a 40-year-old independent research artist living with his vacuum robot in a small studio (but pretty central). He is a-okay, don’t worry about this unhinged post, I’m just kiddin’, I’m still so jetlagged.

item.title: Ratfucker AI
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: We’ll probably soon see much more AI-enabled ratfucking (automated opposition research on mostly true material), powered by decision models and LLMs, and I predict a decent chance of a…
item.content:encoded:
We’ll probably soon see much more AI-enabled ratfucking (automated opposition research on mostly true material), powered by decision models and LLMs, and I predict a decent chance of a Ratfuckopocalypse next year that might dominate the media cycle and have national security implications. Like, think about it, for example soon every intern with too much access can say something like:  

“@Claude: Go through the entire slack/intranet and tell me what the worst thing people have done at this company in the past.”

The AIs will dig up a lot of kompromat.

It’s starting already, cf someone used AI to collect the ‘most damning quotes’ and mapped the funding of EAs – in their own words.

Decision models like Jev are up to ~2 OOMs cheaper than frontier LLMs, and so far ~nobody has spelled out what that means: you can run a yes/no “is this damning?” filter over millions of messages, emails and documents for a few dollars, then hand the hits to a stronger LLM to connect the dots.

Some of the scandals might be justified, others might not. Small world networks and few degrees of separation between any one mean that anyone can be accused of being guilty by virtue of association. Like, did you know Dario Amodei’s wife once started a porn company and pitched it to Jeffrey Epstein, the pedo, for investment? I read it in the WSJ recently. Most often there’s more to the stories than the headlines suggest, or like in this case it’s a nothingburger, but few people read past the headlines, and headlines might be enough to stir things up and create controversy.

This probably has nat sec implications, with state actors leaking or amplifying kompromat and this just became much less expensive. Remember how Germany’s minister for defence lost his job because he plagiarized in his doctoral thesis? There were about a dozen other high-profile cases like that at the minister level in Europe in recent years and that’s just with access to their publicly published theses using crowdsourced wikis.

The scandals might also flood the zone and polarize society and cause anomie:

Perhaps this might also influence elections and lead to more populism.

Perhaps there’ll be lots of ransomware coming too. It also intersects with weak cybersecurity.

Maybe the vibe will shift even further away from cancel culture and people will mellow a bit more and move towards  ‘judge not lest you be judged’ or they’ll realize that morality is surprisingly detailed. People might start to become more privacy focused and record less information. It’s unclear what can be done about this aside from speeding up this process. And I haven’t seen much discussion about this but it seems that it might potentially be a fairly big deal.

On the other hand, maybe this will be bottlenecked by attention, not dirt, and after a few massive drops people will get scandal fatigue.

It doesn’t seem like we need any further technical advances for that and, in contradistinction to say bio- or cybersecurity, AI companies might not be able to put in ‘safety filters’ here.  I think this might potentially be really big.

item.title: Reading too many posts causes premature cognitive decline
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: I can’t quite remember exactly where and when I noticed it the first time, which is ironic, but it must have been when I was merely around 33 years old and I also I do remember the event itself very…
item.content:encoded:
I can’t quite remember exactly where and when I noticed it the first time, which is ironic, but it must have been when I was merely around 33 years old and I also I do remember the event itself very vividly: I was watching a documentary that was a little bit meh but everyone was talking about it and it had such a high RT score when around halfway through the film there was a BIG OL’ reveal: the documentarian uncovered a tickle torture porn ring! But it was not the tickle torture porn ring that took me by surprise, but that I had seen the exact same film before and forgotten the entire set-up and everything leading up to the big reveal.

How-oh-how could I have forgotten that tickle torture porn ring? How was that possible? Do I fashion myself an infovore and a man of culture? Yes. And yes, I have seen that Werner Herzog movie where the guy gets eaten by the bear. True, maybe I did watch too many movies then and it all became a bit of a blur but it wasn’t that that many. Do I love drinking? Well, also yes, but not so much that my axons were demyelinating. Was I just an old baldy then? Well, I was but I was hiding it well and I did get MSP. And I was only a third of a century old; why-oh-why was this shit already starting at this age?

My undergraduate major in social and cognitive psychology (a discipline now mostly discredited), too, is a bit hazy, but this was partly the concerta and partly because my English was still developing and there’s a strong relationship between language and memory. I do distinctly remember an experiment from undergraduate psychology about the causes of childhood amnesia being due to the lack of language development where they showed young kids like some really memorable event and they found that only the kids who had the words to verbalize it could recall it at a later stage. Would it replicate? ‘I want to believe’.

But the other thing I remember from that course on memory is that the reason for why we ‘forget’ things as we age. It’s not that we actually forget things, it’s that we mostly have trouble recalling.

When you’re very young, you only know one of white male actor, say Matt Daemon, because all you’ve watched is Good Will Hunting. But then you watch too many movies and you know so many white male actors, and when you try to retrieve it there’s a certain probability mass on each of them. What was his name again, that actor, what’s his face, the guy who played Bond after Pierce Brosnan? You’re pretty sure it’s not Michael Cera, but there it could be so many others that roughly fit the bill.

It’s unsettling, but you learn to live with it. You start masking ‘Oh yeah long time no see, how’s it going ehem…  oh, yeah, I remember you, but you have so many meetings at EAG.’  It’s not early-onset Alzheimer’s, but it’s not not early onset Alzheimer’s either, in that it’s progressive and spreads to other areas of life outside of film trivia. Like, true, you’ve always been a ladies man and you don’t have to brag, but it wasn’t that many (indeed far too few), yet never had you thought you’d forget any of them, but then you did (it’s good that you keep a list, again, not because there were so many, but due to my issue with the retrieval).

So what to do about it? Maybe it’s all just too much. Too much gunk, gunking up your brain. You need to unsubscribe. Unsubscribe from everything. Clear out the cache. Do a reboot, make room for new stuff, but be more selective. Maybe it’s time to settle down. No more Feeld (not that it’s ever been easy there), no more South Park. Get back on the horse, get back on Hinge, find a wife, and only watch the highbrow stuff, the stuff that’s edifying, only the major HBO shows. Only what Tyler Cowen recommends, nothing Scaruffi rates less than 7.2 or maybe 6.9. But even that’s too much isn’t it? And besides it’s too dry and heavy. There’s too much content that’s for sure. Maybe I could use spaced repetition to drill and solidify the facts about friends and loved ones and my godchildren and then I could play GTA VI when it comes out.

Maybe go to Inkhaven, read the greats. One of the organizers read thousands of essays, and he seems pretty stable still. But on some level that seems insane to me. Everyone’s writing so much… who has the time and wherewithal to read all of that?

I mean does anyone even subvocalize anymore? Are you really savouring the fiction you read? Or are we all merely skimming at this stage. Just getting through it. Come on Proust, just get to the god damn point already. What's the bottom line? BLUF! Apparently, Marcel becomes a novelist.

Do you ‘member when you were young and it was so joyous to read novels? Took your sweet time reading all those novels, didn’t ya? Subvocalized. Yeah, I ‘member. But do you remember when you first tried to get into speed reading in college? They gave you all these readings and then there were even optional readings but it's just too much. You spend hours in the library and you can't possibly get all the reading done. But maybe you're a completionist. You start doing the math: 'well I read 14 pages this hour, and the syllabus has x, and there are y courses so, how do I get through all the reading? How would anyone? Even your literature professor says ‘Even if you read 100 books a year, that’s just at most a few thousands during your life time.’ Your college girlfriend says the professor gives her the creeps. Not in a harrassy way but one time they had a meeting his glasses cracked for no apparent reason. He was kind of weird that guy. Why was he reading all these books for? I guess he was teaching literature. You start thinking: maybe I'm a slow reader... is there a way to speed that up? You look into speed reading. They tell you not to subvocalise. They tell you subvocalisation is the devil. They tell you subvocalization is for the actually imbecilic. But it's just kind of skimming. But like... aren't thoughts words? How would you not subvocalise? Apparently, ‘language is primarily a tool for communication rather than thought’, there was a Nature paper that I meant to read. But is that true for wordcels? Is speed-reading all bs like hypnosis? I remember they did test them on some tv show and gave some speed readers long books and asked them questions and they answered them correctly. But maybe they were just using some really high-level heuristics? There are probably no good papers on that. I call bs. Like sure you can skim. You get better at skimming with age too, especially w/ stuff that is highly structured like scientific papers. But the entropy in good literature should be sufficiently high that makes skimming somewhat pointless. It's like listening to podcasts and audiobooks. Some nonfiction I can listen to at 3x the speed because it's just so nonfiction drivel that doesn't cause much surprisal at all. But then literature... Why would you speed read that at all? Just to get the cliff notes? Why not read 'save the cat' and learn about the basics of narrative. I've never read 'save the cat' but I've always wanted to. Maybe if I had a more abstract theory of how narrative works I could be more like von Neumann? Or at least like Lena Dunham… she said Jenny Koenner told her everything about b-story lines and stuff. Meow.

A related thought I had about this recently (suave segway): what's the deal w/ all these kids who are like in their early 20s having like this agenda to have the most sophisticated taste in art possible by just approaching it really systematically and just read what Tyler Cowen and Scaruffi recommend? That's kind of fucked up. I was talking to one of these kids once and it seems like they've listened to everything and seen all the important films, but like, it does seem a bit weird. Don't you have to watch some bad movies sometime or discover stuff through serendipity? Don’t you need live experience? One of them said their favourite FJM song is ‘Leaving LA’. As if. Isn’t art kinda subjective or something? Isn't the best music the music that you listen to during formative moments of your life, like when that older american woman living above you recommends the magnetic fields? God she was fiiiine. First time you saw her you couldn’t stop staring and things happened because you still had fantasies and could act on your desires. Now you’re on SSRIs and GLP-1s and you’re like bread on a stick. Even friggin’ TLP tells you to read the primary sources, but maybe: fuck that? Maybe I don’t want to be led by TLP anymore. Maybe that’s the lesson. I just need to get my fantasies and healthy desire back. It’s all noise. It’s all too much. What do all these dead white guys know anyway. Didn’t they believe that women had more teeth than men and we should set widows on fire and isn’t that suggestive evidence that are wrong in all the other important ways as well? And it’s all so heavy and dry. I say: don’t read the research digests either. Brevity comes from selection not compression.

Don’t read anything at all I guess is the lesson. There, I said it. Touch some grass maybe. Writing on the other hand. Oh yes, writing is thinking. The stuff of thought. Start creating, stop consuming. But then what should you write about? I need inspiration. I recently came across the wikipedia article on philosophical fiction. Tempting no? Maybe I am in the market for a new novel after all. Or maybe I should give Knausgaard another try, I guess he’s in my reference class, but then what does he know? Maybe more Rachel Cusk. Maybe read only women, but not performatively. Like read even more Cusk but don’t tell anyone. Anybody got any good reading recommendations? Let me know in the comments. ba dum tsssssss 🥁.

Frerk, is a 40-year-old independent research artist living with his vacuum robot in a small studio (but pretty central). He is a-okay, don’t worry about this unhinged post, I’m just kiddin’, I’m just jetlagged.
